usage.callShape: POST https://scrapepay.melis.ai/scrape with JSON body {url, format?, selector?, wait_for?, timeout_ms?}
usage.outputShape: body.success (bool), body.url, body.content (extracted page text/html/markdown), body.word_count — per the 402's advertised example output (NOT verified — payment never settled)
quirks: UNPAYABLE VIA OUR STACK: both qa-pay.mjs and mcp__sponge__paid_fetch fail with 'Failed to parse payment requirements: Invalid payment required response' on this endpoint's 402.

The 402 itself is a structurally valid x402 v2 exact-scheme response (network=base, asset=USDC 0x8335...2913, payTo=0x1C68...B3bC, maxAmountRequired=10000 = $0.01 fixed). Sponge's parser rejects it anyway — likely choking on the nested per-accepts outputSchema, the top-level resource object, or extensions.bazaar.
Price is FIXED at $0.01 (not 'Varies' as the registry surface claims).
No money was spent on either attempt (paid:false both times). 0 paid attempts.
Endpoint server is healthy (HTTP/2 402, Caddy+Express, returns clean JSON challenge) — the defect is a payment-provider/parser incompatibility, not a dead route.
usage.guide: ScrapePay is a $0.01-per-call x402 web scraper: POST a JSON body with {url} (optional format=text|html|markdown, selector, wait_for, timeout_ms) and you should get back {success, url, content, word_count}. HOWEVER it is currently UNPAYABLE through our wallet stack: both the qa-pay primitive and Sponge paid_fetch fail to parse its (otherwise valid x402 v2) 402 challenge with 'Failed to parse payment requirements: Invalid payment required response'. Do not route real spend here until the Sponge payment parser is fixed to accept its accepts[].outputSchema / top-level resource / extensions.bazaar fields, or a different x402 client is used. No funds were lost during testing.
